text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: gpu-inference-prod reports surge of 429s and queue growth. alert: 15% 429 rate over last 5m, QPS spike 4x, GPU pool hotpath exhausted. Auto-escalate to oncall. thread_ts=1779999999

maya (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing metrics + runbook. first check: are autoscaler or ratepolicies saturated?

arjun (sre): seeing queue length ~12k reqs, hotpath pool utilization 98%. autoscaler stuck at pool max=4 instances (we have scale_limit configured in reserved policy). tokens per second for tier-high seems miscalculated after yesterday's ratepolicy rollout. related logs: `rate-limiter: token_refill=500/s tier=high buckets=4` but actual ingress shows refill ~50/s due to units mismatch.

liz (eng-runtime): that unit mismatch came from the new tier config that used "tokens_per_minute" field instead of "tokens_per_second" — config parser defaulted to seconds but the CSV import used minutes. it silently created throttles.

maya (oncall): timeline: around 10:12 UTC we saw QPS jump >4x, autoscaler heartbeat healthy but couldn't scale because per-pool max_nodes=4. at 10:14 429s started rising. can we open emergency capacity?

arjun (sre): attempting emergency pool resize. command: ```bash
# increase GPU pool max to 8 (temporary)
redwoodctl pools update gpu-hotpath --max-nodes 8 --reason "emergency 429 mitigation"
```

deploy-bot: runbook step executed by maya: `pools.update started` (task id: task-0a9b).

liz (eng-runtime): while scaling will help, tokens will still starve higher-tier requests because tier enforcement weight is too low. propose quick tokenbucket tune: bump refill multiplier for "tier-high" and relax strict-tier-enforcement.

arjun (sre): sending API patch to rate-limiter: ```bash
curl -sS -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/ratepolicies/gpu-hotpath/patch" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"patch": [{"op":"replace","path":"/tiers/high/refill_rate","value":1000},{"op":"replace","path":"/tiers/high/enforce_strict","value":false}] }'
```

arjun (sre): applied patch, validating. logs now show token_refill=1000/s for tier-high. watching 429 rate.

maya (oncall): can we also open a temporary fallback route to CPU inference pool for non-latency-critical traffic? that'll relieve GPU queue pressure.

liz (eng-runtime): routing rule change ready: ```yaml
- match: path == "/v1/generate" && model.family == "gpt-neox"
  action: route_to: [gpu-hotpath, cpu-backfill]
  priority: 50
  fallback_policy: prefer_gpu_but_allow_cpu
``` applying now.

paul (cust-success): heads-up — customers with reserved Dedicated capacity may see increased latency while we divert. I'll start notifying top affected customers (acct: neatAI, docsFlow). message draft: "We're currently mitigating an inference capacity issue; you may experience higher latency for a short window. We'll follow up with a timeline and postmortem."

maya (oncall): after the two changes (scale-up + tokenbucket patch + route fallback) 429s dropped from 15% -> 2% within 6 minutes. queue drained to ~1.8k. GPU utilization at 80% now. good.

arjun (sre): root cause hypothesis: config import for tier policies used minutes vs seconds units; combined with conservative pool max_nodes prevented autoscaler from compensating. chain: tokenbucket undervalued -> more requests throttled -> clients retried -> queue grows -> autoscaler reached config cap -> more 429s. also observed priority inversion where mid-tier got higher share due to wrong weights.

liz (eng-runtime): longer-term fixes: validate config import to reject ambiguous units, add e2e test to simulate surge and assert token refill rates, add autoscaler alert when pool at 95%+ and queue growth rate > threshold despite scaling attempts.

maya (oncall): immediate follow-ups: 1) revert route change after stabilization (in 30m) 2) keep gpu-hotpath max_nodes=8 for next 2 hours then roll to configured value with controlled backfill testing 3) escalate to eng-runtime for config import fix 4) open postmortem with timeline + customers impacted. Who owns? liz/ arjun?

liz (eng-runtime): I will own the postmortem; arjun will own immediate infra runbook updates for tokenbucket tuning steps.

paul (cust-success): notified top customers at 10:35 UTC. two customers acknowledged, one asked for SLA credit estimate — will handoff to bizops.

maya (oncall): adding commands for runbook to safe-tune tokenbucket in the short term: ```bash
# show current policy
redwoodctl ratepolicy get gpu-hotpath --name tiers
# quick tune: increase refill and weight for high tier
redwoodctl ratepolicy patch gpu-hotpath --json '[{"op":"replace","path":"/tiers/high/refill_rate","value":1000},{"op":"replace","path":"/tiers/high/weight","value":8}]'
# temporarily disable strict per-tenant enforcement
redwoodctl ratepolicy patch gpu-hotpath --json '[{"op":"replace","path":"/config/enforce_strict","value":false}]'
```

arjun (sre): note: do NOT forget to revert the enforce_strict flag — leaving it off reduces isolation. add a guard in runbook: `--ttl 30m` or schedule automated revert.

deploy-bot: autoscaler task completed: `pool gpu-hotpath scaled to 7 nodes` (target 8 in-progress).

maya (oncall): handing off to eng-runtime for root cause and to cust-success for customer comms. oncall to monitor for 60m then close.

liz (eng-runtime): creating postmortem doc: https://internal.redwood/postmortems/1779999999-gpu-tokenbucket-import-misunit (placeholder). collecting traces: https://observability.redwood/trace/abcd1234.

paul (cust-success): putting follow-up to BizOps for SLA impact calculation. tagging billing for potential credits.

maya (oncall): summary for handoff: mitigations applied = [increase pool max -> 8, tokenbucket refill bump for tier-high, route fallback to cpu-backfill]; customer impact = elevated latency & 429s for ~22 minutes for some routed requests, major customers notified. owners: liz (postmortem), arjun (infra runbook), paul (customer comms).

arjun (sre): closing notes: will add a lint rule to config importer to error on ambiguous units and add an alert when a pool is at configured max for >2m with sustained queue growth.

maya (oncall): marking incident as stabilized. will remain in watch for 60m then close and escalate to postmortem. :white_check_mark:
